turns.text:
Back in August I asked my ex if we could swap Thanksgiving this year. My mom turns 70 that week and my family is meeting in Honolulu. I offered him Christmas Eve and Christmas Day in exchange. He wrote back "Probably fine." I said thank you, I'd start looking at flights. He didn't object. Not a word about it for two months.

So in September I booked three tickets, me and our two kids. $2,640, nonrefundable. Then on October 14 he texts that his dad had surgery, he needs the kids for Thanksgiving, and he can't do the swap. I told him I'd already booked. His answer was "I said probably." I called him twice that night. He didn't pick up. At 7:30 the next morning he emails me with our mediator copied, quoting the plan at me. Now he's treating it like a court case. He never said no until I'd paid for it.

I'm sorry about his dad, I really am. But I think he's using it to get back at me for leaving. My mom only turns 70 once. I'm gutted, and I don't know what to tell the kids.

Am I wrong to hold him to the swap?

You are not wrong to feel blindsided. You are on thin ground if "hold him to the swap" means taking the kids to Honolulu against the parenting plan.

"Probably fine" is a hedge. You heard a yes and acted on it. He can point at that word and say he never agreed. Two months of silence after you said you were booking flights still matters: he knew you were spending the money and he let it sit. That was a bad way to co-parent. It does not turn "probably" into a signed change to the plan. Once he copied the mediator and quoted the order, he put this back on the written schedule. Nonrefundable tickets rarely override that.

His dad's surgery can be real and the timing can still feel punitive. Lead with the surgery as real. If you tell the mediator this is revenge for leaving, you hand him the cleaner story: medical need, the order, and you minimizing his father.

Reply on the email he already opened, short and factual. Dates only: you asked in August, he said "probably fine," you said you would book, he said nothing, you bought the tickets in September, he withdrew in October. Ask the mediator to help you find a split that still gets the kids to your mom for part of that week, and offer Christmas exactly as you already did. Ask whether a shorter Honolulu trip, one child going, or him taking them for the surgery window and you having the birthday itself is possible. Check change fees and credits before you decide the $2,640 is gone.

Do not put the kids on a plane if his Thanksgiving time is what the plan gives him and he has now said no. That is the move that makes you the one who broke the order.

With the kids, keep it small and do not make them the jury. Their grandfather had surgery, Thanksgiving with Dad is the plan this year, and you are working on another way to be with Grandma for her birthday. They do not need "he said probably" or why you left.

You are right that he handled this badly. You are not right that the swap is locked in.

He said "probably," stayed quiet while you bought nonrefundable tickets, and only said no after the money was spent. That is unfair, and you can say so to the mediator with the dates.

The parenting plan still controls his Thanksgiving time unless you both change it. "Probably," plus silence, is not that change. Taking the kids anyway would make you the one who broke the order.
